# Sensitivity analyses: other covariates, post-spawn temperatures and the Big Creek gradient

```{r a6-load}
F5 <- rev_tab("F5_elevation_sensitivity.csv")
span <- rev_tab("F5_elevation_span_by_stream.csv")
T1 <- rev_tab("Table_01_rev.csv")
f5a <- F5 |> filter(data == "All streams")
f5b <- F5 |> filter(data == "Without Big Creek")
f5c <- F5 |> filter(grepl("split", data))
E2 <- rev_tab("E2_post_spawn_indices.csv")
E2v <- rev_tab("E2_post_spawn_index_values.csv")
```

We tested whether reach elevation, reach slope, discharge or temperatures after spawning explained spawn timing beyond the final model. Results are in `R/09_refit-fixed-date-model.R` (F5), `R/08_fixed-date-index.R` (E2) and Table 1 of the main text.

## Elevation

Elevation is fixed for each reach, so it can only compete with the between-reach component of temperature ($\bar{T}$; Section A4). Added to the final model, elevation improved fit by `r sprintf("%.0f", -f5a$dAIC_adding_E)` AIC units: higher reaches spawned `r sprintf("%.1f", -f5a$E_per100m)` days earlier per 100 m (SE `r sprintf("%.1f", f5a$E_se)`), and the between-reach temperature effect fell from `r sprintf("%.1f", f5a$T_bar_noE)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", f5a$T_bar_withE)` days per °C (@tbl-a6-elev). The within-reach temperature effect was unchanged (`r sprintf("%.1f", f5a$T_dev_withE)` days per °C).

This effect depends on one stream. Surveyed reaches in Big Creek span `r sprintf("%.0f", span$span_m[span$stream == "Big"])` m of elevation, compared with `r sprintf("%.0f", min(span$span_m[span$stream != "Big"]))`--`r sprintf("%.0f", max(span$span_m[span$stream != "Big"]))` m elsewhere (@tbl-a1-survey). Without Big Creek, elevation had no detectable effect (`r sprintf("%.1f", f5b$E_per100m)` days per 100 m, SE `r sprintf("%.1f", f5b$E_se)`) and did not improve fit (ΔAIC = `r sprintf("%+.1f", f5b$dAIC_adding_E)`). Allowing separate elevation slopes gave `r sprintf("%.1f", f5c$E_big)` (SE `r sprintf("%.1f", f5c$E_big_se)`) days per 100 m in Big Creek and `r sprintf("%.1f", f5c$E_others)` (SE `r sprintf("%.1f", f5c$E_others_se)`) elsewhere (@fig-a6-elev). We therefore did not include elevation in the final model.

Within Big Creek, upper reaches spawned earlier than their summer temperatures predict, and lower reaches later. Several explanations fit this single gradient and cannot be separated with these data: run-timing structure (summer-run fish spawn in lower Big Creek; Copeland et al. 2019), migration distance or arrival order, and colder fall and winter incubation conditions in upper reaches (post-spawn indices behaved the same way as elevation; Section A6.2).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-a6-elev
#| tbl-cap: "Elevation added to the final model, with all streams and without Big Creek. Temperature effects ($\\bar{T}$, reach mean; $T-\\bar{T}$, reach-year anomaly) in days per °C; SE in parentheses."
F5 |>
  filter(!grepl("split", data)) |>
  transmute(
    Data = data,
    `$\\bar{T}$, no elevation` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", T_bar_noE, T_bar_noE_se),
    `$\\bar{T}$, with elevation` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", T_bar_withE, T_bar_withE_se),
    `$T-\\bar{T}$, with elevation` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", T_dev_withE, T_dev_withE_se),
    `Elevation (d per 100 m)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", E_per100m, E_se),
    `ΔAIC adding elevation` = sprintf("%+.1f", dAIC_adding_E)
  ) |>
  kbl(booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "", align = "lrrrrr", escape = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling(font_size = 8) |>
  column_spec(2:6, width = "2.1cm")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-a6-elev
#| fig-cap: "Reach random intercepts from the final model (no elevation) against reach elevation, for Big Creek and the other streams. Lines: linear fits. Positive intercepts = later spawning than temperature, stream and year predict."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.2
re_e <- ranef(final)$COMID |>
  rownames_to_column("COMID") |>
  rename(intercept = `(Intercept)`) |>
  left_join(d |> distinct(COMID = as.character(COMID), stream, elev), by = "COMID") |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(stream == "Big", "Big Creek", "Other streams"))
ggplot(re_e, aes(elev, intercept)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(color = stream), size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.streams) +
  labs(x = "Reach elevation (m)", y = "Reach random intercept (d)", color = "Stream")
```

## Post-spawn (incubation) indices

Salmon may time spawning so that fry emerge in a favourable spring window, so that reaches with colder incubation spawn earlier (Heggberget 1988; Brannon et al. 2004). The original submission tested post-spawn windows that began on each redd's own spawn date, which carries the mirror image of the artifact in Section A2. We instead computed fixed-date reach-year means for fall (1 Sep--30 Nov), winter (1 Dec--28 Feb), spring (1 Mar--30 Apr) and the whole incubation period (1 Sep--30 Apr), and the number of days to emergence for a fixed reference spawn date (1 Sep or 15 Aug), using the Beacham and Murray (1990) Chinook emergence model (model 2) as implemented in hatchR (Sparks et al. 2026). For a 1 September spawn, predicted emergence ranged from `r format(as.Date("2002-09-01") + min(E2v$emerge_1Sep), "%d %b")` to `r format(as.Date("2002-09-01") + max(E2v$emerge_1Sep), "%d %b")` among reach-years.

On their own, all post-spawn indices predicted spawn timing in the direction the hypothesis predicts (warmer incubation, later spawning; @tbl-a6-e2). For example, spawn date shifted `r sprintf("%.2f", -E2$slope_alone[E2$index == "emerge_1Sep"])` days earlier for each additional day of predicted incubation, offsetting roughly a quarter of the among-reach difference in development time. However, post-spawn indices were strongly correlated with the pre-spawn index (r up to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(E2$r_with_prespawn_T)))`). When added to the final model they improved fit only because of Big Creek; without Big Creek, none improved fit and their effects were near zero (@tbl-a6-e2). The data are therefore consistent with incubation matching but cannot separate it from the summer thermal regime of a reach (see Section A6.1).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-a6-e2
#| tbl-cap: "Post-spawn (incubation) indices. Alone: spawn date ~ index + stream + year. Added: index added to the final model (Section A4), with all streams and without Big Creek. Slopes are days per °C, or days per day of predicted incubation for emergence indices. Negative ΔAIC = better fit."
E2 |>
  transmute(
    Index = label,
    `r with pre-spawn index` = sprintf("%.2f", r_with_prespawn_T),
    `Alone: slope (SE); ΔAIC vs pre-spawn` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f); %+.1f", slope_alone, se_alone, dAIC_alone_vs_prespawn_T),
    `Added to final: slope (SE); ΔAIC` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f); %+.1f", slope_added, se_added, dAIC_added_vs_final),
    `Added, no Big Creek: slope (SE); ΔAIC` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f); %+.1f", slope_added_noBig, se_added_noBig, dAIC_added_vs_final_noBig)
  ) |>
  kbl(booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "", align = "lrrrr") |>
  kable_styling(font_size = 8) |>
  column_spec(1, width = "3.6cm") |>
  column_spec(3:5, width = "2.9cm")
```

## Reach slope

Reach slope ranged narrowly (`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * min(d$slope))`--`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * max(d$slope))`%) and did not improve the final model (ΔAIC = `r sprintf("%+.1f", T1$dAIC[T1$Model == "+ reach slope"])`; Table 1 of the main text).

## Discharge

Discharge was available only from one gauge downstream of all study reaches (USGS 13309220), so it varies among years but not among reaches, and it is confounded with the year effect. Discharge summaries in the original submission were also computed over windows anchored to each redd's spawn date and so share the artifact in Section A2. We did not retain discharge.

```{r}
#| label: fig-a6-flow
#| fig-cap: "Mean daily discharge at the Middle Fork Salmon River gauge near Middle Fork Lodge (USGS 13309220), 2002–2005."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3
read_csv(here("data", "processed", "mfsr_flow.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  transmute(date = as.Date(Date), flow = Flow) |>
  filter(year(date) %in% 2002:2005, format(date, "%m-%d") != "02-29") |>
  mutate(year = factor(year(date)), doy = std_doy(date)) |>
  ggplot(aes(fixed_date + doy, flow, color = year)) +
  annotate("rect",
    xmin = fixed_date + min(redds$yday), xmax = fixed_date + max(redds$yday),
    ymin = 0, ymax = Inf, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.years) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = expression(Discharge ~ (ft^3 ~ s^-1)), color = "Year")
```
